title: Punctual bound suffices for a module bound
statement:
Let $(V,F)$ be a finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-Frobenius module in the
sense of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] such that every
eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$ satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|\leq q^{w/2}$.
Then $(V,F)$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$.

proof.text: Fix the coefficient data, $q>1$, and $w$ from [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. We prove the claim for every Frobenius module with the asserted eigenvalue bound by strong induction on $n=\dim_{\Qlb}V$. If $n=0$, then $V=0$ and the length-zero filtration, with no weights or graded pieces, satisfies the definition of mixedness. In the induction step assume the claim for every module of dimension less than $n$.

source.place: Proof, construction of the finite stable filtration; dimension-zero case

proof.text: If $n>0$, apply [lem-zl-alg-closed-endomorphism-eigenvalue] with the algebraically closed field $\Qlb$, nonzero finite-dimensional space $V$, and endomorphism $F$. Obtain $v\ne0$ and $\alpha$ with $Fv=\alpha v$. Since $F$ is injective, $\alpha\ne0$. Set $L=\Qlb v$. For each scalar $c$, $F(cv)=c\alpha v$, and $F(c\alpha^{-1}v)=cv$, so $F(L)=L$. The inverse acts on $L$ by $\alpha^{-1}$; consequently both $F$ and its inverse descend to $C=V/L$. Inclusion and the quotient map give a Frobenius-equivariant short exact sequence $0\to L\to V\to C\to0$: the quotient map is surjective with kernel $L$ by [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module].

source.place: Proof, eigenvector and its stable span

proof.text: The map $\Qlb\to L$, $c\mapsto cv$, is surjective by the definition of $L$ and injective because $v\ne0$; thus $v$ is a basis of $L$ and $\dim L=1$. The images of any finite spanning set of $V$ span $C$, so $C$ is finite-dimensional. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] to the quotient map $\pi:V\to C$ of step 2: by [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] $\pi$ is surjective with kernel $L$, so $\operatorname{Im}(\pi)=C$ and $\ker(\pi)=L$, and the lemma gives $\dim C+1=n$, hence $\dim C<n$.

source.place: Proof, finite-dimensional termination of the stable filtration

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence] to the equivariant short exact sequence in step 2. Every eigenvalue $\beta$ of the induced automorphism on $C$ has $\iota(\beta)$ in its spectrum, hence in that of $V$. Since $\iota$ is injective, $\beta$ itself is an eigenvalue of $F$, and therefore $|\iota(\beta)|\leq q^{w/2}$. The module $C$ has the same coefficient data and smaller dimension, so the strong induction hypothesis makes $C$ mixed of weights at most $w$.

source.place: Proof, graded eigenvalues inherited from the original module by the spectrum lemma

proof.text: Put $r=|\iota(\alpha)|$. Nonvanishing of $\alpha$ and injectivity of $\iota$ give $r>0$. Define $t=2\log_q r$. Apply [lem-a1-real-logarithm-power] with $b=q>1$, $x=r>0$, and $y=w/2$. It gives $q^{t/2}=q^{\log_q r}=r$ and, from the assumed bound $r\leq q^{w/2}$, $\log_q r\leq w/2$. Multiplying by $2>0$ yields $t\leq w$.

source.place: Proof, assignment of the real weight 2 log_q of the nonzero eigenvalue modulus

proof.text: Every nonzero vector of $L$ is $cv$ with $c\ne0$. If it is a $\beta$-eigenvector, then $c\alpha v=F(cv)=\beta cv$; cancellation of the nonzero scalar $c$ and vector $v$ gives $\beta=\alpha$. Step 5 therefore proves that every eigenvalue on $L$ has modulus $q^{t/2}$, so $L$ is pure of weight $t$ by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. The filtration $0\subseteq L$ has only the quotient $L/0$, identified with $L$ by $[x]\mapsto x$; this map intertwines the induced automorphism because it sends $[Fx]$ to $Fx$. Since $t\leq w$, this filtration makes $L$ mixed of weights at most $w$.

source.place: Proof, pure simple pieces and the filtration witnessing mixedness

proof.text: In $0\to L\to V\to C\to0$, both outer terms are mixed of weights at most $w$ by steps 4 and 6. All maps are equivariant and the sequence is short exact by step 2. Apply [lem-a1-extension-bounds] to deduce that $V$ is mixed of weights at most $w$. This completes the strong induction.

source.place: Proof, assembly of the finite stable filtration from the eigenline and quotient

proof_origin.place: Entire proof: explicit eigenline and quotient induction realizing the stable-filtration argument, with spectrum inheritance and real weights as in the blueprint.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q118-91139206d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and fixed one duplicate node. The statement is identical to the blueprint in both snapshots (master order 2788, main-20261015 order 3132) and is not weakened. The proof writes out the blueprint's Jordan–Hölder argument as a strong induction on dim V: split off an eigenline L, apply induction to the quotient C = V/L, then join the two with lem-a1-extension-bounds. I checked every step against the cited statements. The induction is set up properly, with the case V=0 handled by m=0. α≠0 because F is injective, and F(L)=L both ways, so F and its inverse pass to C. For C, lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence plus injectivity of ι means C's eigenvalues are eigenvalues of F, so they keep the bound. Step 5 uses Mathlib's Real.rpow_logb (Log/Base.lean 146–148) and Real.logb_le_iff_le_rpow (206–207), whose hypotheses b>1 and x>0 hold. I tested V=0, a scalar module with |ι(α)|<1 and negative w, a Jordan block, and a diagonal module with different moduli; all work. There is no cycle: no cited node's dependency closure contains the item. Fault (C5): the new node lem-a1-quotient-dimension duplicates the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity, applied to the quotient map V→C, which is surjective with kernel L by def-weil-pbc-quotient-module. It also wrote out 'dimension' instead of citing def-weil-vector-space-dimension. I dropped it and rewrote step 3 and proof_deps to cite the existing node; nothing else cited it. The other new node, lem-a1-real-logarithm-power, is a correct, self-contained two-declaration Mathlib leaf with no duplicate in the DAG; accepted. Batch-5 check: lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence reaches sk-def-frobmod only through def-weil-frobenius-module-weights, which cites it just for what a Frobenius module is. That is a general definition, not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, and the spectrum lemma is characteristic-polynomial linear algebra, so I accepted it. No tool_uses are needed; the route goes through sk-l-dl-a1-endpoints, which the unit uses.
